Subject: Observability onboarding — dashboard & trace priority matrix

Hi Lydia —

Thanks again for the time today. As discussed, we want to align on a small, deliverable onboarding scope that wins early value for your platform monitoring and keeps the implementation sprint tight. Attached is a lightweight template we use (runbook + dashboard matrix) and an initial list of tracing hooks we typically instrument during the first 2 weeks.

Proposal (high level):
- Week 0: kickoff + review of your current monitoring matrix (you mentioned a CSV)
- Week 1: deploy core dashboards (latency, error-rate, token-cost burn) + tracing hooks for request path and model-call correlation
- Week 2: alert routing, runbook drafts, and a 60-minute operational warroom to validate alerts on synthetic load

Can you send the current monitoring matrix (dashboards, alerts, owners) and confirm who from your infra team will join the kickoff? If you prefer, we can limit week 1 to a single dashboard + one trace-span correlation to unblock product on-call.

Attachments: acme_monitoring_matrix.csv (if available), redwood_runbook_template_v1.pdf, trace-hook-list.md

Best,
Rachel

Hi Lydia / Rachel —

Reviewing the CSV. Nice work — this gives us a clear place to start. A couple of operational asks from our side to make the sprint predictable: 
- Can Acme grant a read-only service account to the dashboard data source for the onboarding window? This avoids chasing credentials and speeds validation.
- Please flag which alerts are "P0" vs "P1" vs "informational" in column G of the CSV so we can prioritize.

Deliverables we’ll produce during the two-week kickoff:
1) A condensed dashboard pack (3-5 tiles): request latency p50/p95, model-call latency, token burn per route, error taxonomy heatmap
2) Tracing hooks that correlate HTTP request -> model request ID -> model response (span names and attributes in trace-hook-list.md)
3) Runbook drafts to sit next to each alert, plus a suggested on-call escalation path (pager -> Slack channel -> engineering leader)

I’ve attached our runbook template and a short trace-hook checklist. Aditya — can you confirm the SDK compatibility list and if any quick patch is expected for v1.9?

-Marissa

> I’ve attached our runbook template and a short trace-hook checklist. Aditya — can you confirm the SDK compatibility list and if any quick patch is expected for v1.9?

Quick compatibility notes:
- v1.9 is compatible with the tracing hooks we propose; no SDK upgrade required for basic span/context propagation.
- We recommend a small opt-in patch (server-side middleware, ~15 LOC) to attach model_request_id as a tag on the base request span so trace linking is stable across retries. I can provide a patch snippet and a short test harness.
- Risk: the change is non-blocking and feature-flag safe; it can be deployed to a canary host first.

I uploaded the trace-hook checklist and a minimal patch snippet to the drive link in related_links. If you want, we can add Diego Rivera to the drive for visibility.

Aditya
